issues.legal_issue: A later rent-control provision giving a tenant relief for curing a lease-condition breach applies to pending eviction proceedings under the repealed rent-control law when it clarifies or slightly modifies a remedy already available under that law.
material_facts: The eviction proceedings were pending under the earlier rent-control law when the later law came into force.
The later law expressly permitted relief where a tenant complied with the relevant condition or paid compensation directed by the Controller.
The earlier law required prior notice for eviction based on the relevant lease-condition breach, and the court held that relief for curing the breach could already be available under that law.
issues.conclusion: The later provision was clarificatory and slightly modificatory, rather than a radical departure, and therefore applied to the pending proceedings under the first proviso to section 57(2).
issues.legal_principle: Under section 57(2) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, pending proceedings ordinarily continue under the repealed Act, but the first proviso requires regard to the new Act's provisions where they slightly modify or clarify the earlier law. In Karam Singh v. Sri Pratap Chand, the Court held that this proviso does not displace the general rule that the old Act governs pending proceedings when the new law makes a radical departure; clarifications and slight modifications are to be applied. The Court found that section 14(11) clarified and slightly modified relief already available under section 13(1)(k) of the 1952 Act.

predicates.pending_case_under_repealed_rent_law: An eviction proceeding under an earlier rent-control law remained pending when a later rent-control law came into force.
predicates.later_law_adds_relief_for_same_kind_of_b: The later rent-control law provides relief to a tenant who cures the kind of breach underlying the eviction claim.
predicates.earlier_law_already_allowed_comparable_r: The earlier rent-control law allowed a court to grant comparable relief against eviction for that kind of breach.

issues.definition: When a pending eviction case under an earlier rent-control law concerns a breach for which that law already allowed comparable relief, a later law's added relief for the same kind of breach applies if it clarifies or slightly modifies that existing relief.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant who remedies a notified breach of a lease condition during or before an eviction suit may receive relief from eviction where the notice did not allow a reasonable time to remedy the breach.
material_facts: The landlords sought eviction because tenants had made or maintained structures contrary to conditions imposed on the landlords in their leases.
The authorities notified the landlords about the structures, and the landlords asked the tenants to remove them before bringing suit.
During the proceedings, the tenants removed or altered the offending structures; in one case the remaining wire-gauze net was not treated as an unauthorised construction.
The Court considered whether relief was available under the earlier rent-control law even though it contained no provision corresponding expressly to section 14(11) of the later law.
issues.conclusion: The earlier rent-control law did not prevent a court from granting relief against eviction when a tenant remedied the breach; such relief could be granted where the notice did not allow a reasonable time to do so.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13(1)(k) of the Delhi and Ajmer Rent Control Act, 1952 required previous notice for eviction based on use contrary to a condition imposed on the landlord. The Court relied by analogy on section 114A of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, which permits relief against forfeiture for a remediable breach where the lessee is not given a reasonable time to remedy it. It also referred to Uma Kumari v. Jaswant Rai Chopra in describing the analogy between the notice requirement and relief against forfeiture. Whether the time allowed was reasonable is a question of fact.

predicates.pending_rent_eviction_proceeding_under_p: An eviction proceeding under an earlier rent-control law was pending before the court.
predicates.landlord_claimed_ejectment_for_notified_: The landlord sought eviction for the tenant's use contrary to a lease condition imposed on the landlord, after notice of the breach had been given.
predicates.tenant_remedied_breach_before_or_during_: The tenant removed or otherwise remedied the offending condition before the suit or while it was pending.
predicates.notice_failed_to_allow_reasonable_cure_t: The notice did not give the tenant a reasonable time to remedy the breach.
predicates.court_may_grant_relief_from_ejectment: The court may relieve the tenant from eviction.

issues.definition: If an eviction case under an earlier rent-control law concerns a notified lease-condition breach, the tenant remedies it before or during the suit, and the notice gives no reasonable time to cure, the court may grant relief from eviction.
